decisive_items: a posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7, with a maximum thickness of 10 mm that was homogeneously hyperintense on both T1-weighted and T2-weighted sequences, suggestive of fat
ascending spastic weakness of the lower limbs
graded sensory loss below the D10 level
response.rationale: R1 is more specific due to the direct mention of a posterior epidural mass suggestive of fat, which is a key characteristic of spinal epidural lipomatosis. R3, while plausible, is more general and could apply to various conditions causing spinal cord compression.
